newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: MICHAEL FIELD QUITS AS TASMANIA'S LABOR LEADER
The Labor Party in Tasmania has a new leader after Michael Field resigned at a party meeting this morning.
Former union leader, Jim Bacon, was elected to the position unopposed.
Mr Field's future has been under a cloud since the last state election 14 months ago.
He was the second longest serving Labor leader in Australia behind bob Carr in New South Wales.
ABORIGINAL FLAG DESIGNER FIELDS COPYRIGHT FEE FEARS
The designer of the Aboriginal flag says Aboriginal medical and legal services can use the flag without worrying about paying copyright fees.
But Harold Thomas says he's still seeking advice on the other organisations that will be able to use the flag without paying copyright fees.
A Territory Aboriginal Medical organisation has expressed concern about the flag's future use, and has called on Mr Thomas to relinquish his copyright to Aboriginal Australians.
Mr Thomas says the medical and legal service have always been at the forefront of the Aboriginal movement and there has been an understanding the two services were free to use the flag.
PROGRAM TO REMEMBER WAR VETERANS
The Veterans Affairs Minister Bruce Scott says young Australians are not taught enough Australian military history in the education system.
Mr Scott was launching a four-year Federal Government program to remember the sacrifices of Service men and women.
He says the program, Their Service - Our Heritage, will enable all Australians, through a wide range of events, activities and projects, to acknowledge the debt the nation owes to all veterans.
The Minister says people are increasingly forgetting the service given by war veterans, as time passes.
MINER KILLED IN EXPLOSION NAMED
A 47-year-old man has been killed in an explosion at the VICTOR nickel mine at Kambalda, south of Kalgoorlie.
Police say Peter Martin Able of Kambalda died in an explosion in the decline shortly before three o'clock yesterday afternoon.
A spokesman for the Western Mining Corp says two other workers were treated at the Kambalda Nursing Post while a third man is in a stable condition at the Kalgoorlie Regional Hospital.
The four men were involved in blasting operations.
Police and government mining officials are at the scene.
